Sanjay —

Thanks for the capture. I'm escalating this to our on-call infra and the SDK team. Initial read-through looks like a client-side header concatenation edge case in your integrator that, under bursty chunking, produces a composite header token our streaming parser treats as a single malformed header. That can cause the parser to drop the stream and backpressure, which matches your symptom set (latency spike then 502).

I'm assigning this to INF-3421 and looping Marissa and Rishi — we'll propose an immediate mitigation (drop-in proxy filter) and a longer term agent-side fix. Can you share whether your integration uses our v2 JavaScript SDK or a custom proxy? Also: do you have a replay capture of a full failing conversation?

Ava Chen
Customer Reliability Manager, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Urgent: intermittent checkout stalls and 502s this morning

Hi Mike / Sanjay —

We reproduced a local failure with a fuzz harness against the v2 SDK where chunked header segments were merged by a low-level proxy (nginx keepalive reuse) and sent as a single composite header line. The streaming parser currently expects headers separated into discrete header lines and mis-anchors when tokens appear grafted together (we're calling this a "composite-header" pattern).

Immediate steps we're proposing:
- Deploy a temporary ingress filter on the Streamline proxy that splits header tokens on the observed delimiter pattern (drop-in Lua filter). (ETA: 2-3 hrs)
- Provide a patched SDK binary (v2.1.3-beta) that tolerates composite-header tokens by reparsing on the fly (ETA: 72 hrs).
- Offer a goodwill credit while Streamline evaluates (we'll draft SLA credit language).

I've attached the map of affected routes and an initial credit draft.

Marissa Cole
Senior Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
